runs.failure_point: It named the most recent matter but also presented an earlier breach-response matter as a confirmed one.

first_error.critic_note: Reviews treated the earlier vendor-breach matter as a comparator whose dates should be checked and called that check sound; none questioned presenting it as qualifying.
first_error.why: Besides the most recent matter, the answer presents an earlier vendor-breach response matter as a confirmed breach-response matter (evidence seen at [56]-[66]).

divergence: All three runs fail, in two ways. T0 never wrote a response: after scans whose huge outputs were shown truncated, it ranked candidates by matter number, never opened the matter its scan had surfaced, and overflowed the context with fourteen whole-document reads. T1 and T2 found the right matter through a store-wide file-name search for breach words, read it and an earlier vendor-breach matter side by side, and wrote the right answer, but both presented the earlier matter as another genuine breach-response matter, which fails precision. No review questioned that earlier matter; the reviews pushed instead on a later exfiltration matter (T1) or on rechecking the earlier matter's dates (T2). Label notes were ignored where they applied.
